proposal.name: cryptography
proposal.note: The recipe measures solana-bn254 (syscall/solana-bn254), the BN254 field, curve, pairing and Poseidon arithmetic behind Solana's alt_bn128 and sol_poseidon syscalls. It has no dependencies of its own, and on arm64 it runs only its portable backend: the ADX and AVX-512 paths are x86_64 only and chosen at compile time. There are three cachegrind instruction-count metrics, each with an --inputs-only fixed command: circom Poseidon hashes over widths 2 to 13 (227M instructions), G1/G2 scalar multiplication by full 256-bit scalars with syscall encode/decode (272M), and pairing checks over 2 to 5 pairs (150M). Inputs come only from a seeded splitmix64, and less than 0.5% of each count is harness work. In the trial all three counts gave identical results on both runs (cv 0). 243 upstream tests pass, run through libtest with --lib --tests. The equivalence harness prints, on seeded inputs: Poseidon digests for valid inputs, wrong-length inputs and unreduced inputs. It prints G1/G2 decoding in both byte orders, covering valid, random and flagged encodings. It prints addition, negation, multiplication by edge scalars (0, 1, r, r±1, 2^256-1), subgroup checks, pairings and Gt pow/square/inverse. Patches may only change syscall/solana-bn254/src. The in-source test modules are protected blocks, and tests, examples, benches, manifests, the lockfile and toolchain files are protected paths.
